column3: MT 4:17; verses 2–20 of this chapter are MT 5:1–19. “Your foot” is rendered “your steps,” and “they do not know to do evil” as “they do not know they are doing evil.”
Close to the Hebrew; “On your mouth … your heart” is rendered “in word … in thought.”
Close to the Hebrew; “Abundance of business” is rendered “much effort.”
Close to the Hebrew; “There is no pleasure in fools” is rendered “He takes no delight in fools.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Your flesh” is rendered “you,” “the messenger” as “the messenger of God,” and “inadvertence” as “a mistake.”
The Hebrew is elliptical (“for in many dreams and futilities and many words; but fear God”); NASB adds “there is emptiness” and “Rather.”
Close to the Hebrew; “Robbery of justice” is rendered “denial of justice,” and “a high [one] over a high [one]” as “one official … over another official.”
The Hebrew is obscure; NASB renders “After all, a king who cultivates the field is an advantage to the land.” The meaning is uncertain.
Close to the Hebrew; “Silver” is rendered “money.”
Close to the Hebrew; “The sight of his eyes” is rendered “to look on.”
Close to the Hebrew; “The plenty of the rich” is rendered “the full stomach of the rich man.”
Close to the Hebrew; “A severe evil” is rendered “a grievous evil,” and “kept” as “hoarded.”
“A business of evil” is rendered “a bad investment,” and “nothing in his hand” as “nothing to support him.”
Close to the Hebrew; “In his toil” is rendered “from the fruit of his labor.”
Close to the Hebrew; “As he came, so he will go” is rendered “as a man is born, thus will he die.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew; “Beautiful” is rendered “fitting,” “his portion” as “his reward,” and “the number of the days” as “the few years.”
Close to the Hebrew; “His portion” is rendered “his reward.”
Close to the Hebrew; “Remember” is rendered “consider,” “days” as “years,” and “keeping busy with” as “keeps him occupied with.”
